detail:
verdict=deploy-ready; posted and transitioned; caveats:
  - SSOAuthHandler's own logout-before-redirect was not exercised at runtime: this instance has no identity provider, so the SSO callback cannot be driven. The disabled-user callback case is still caught on the next request by DisabledUserLogoutFilter (shown above with a planted OIDC session), but the 'existing user with no tenant group' branch has no filter-level backstop and rests only on the shipped MockMvc test callbackForExistingUserWithNoTenantGroupEndsTheSession, which drives the real handler and real security filter chain.
  - The OIDC-principal evidence used a security context planted directly in Valkey rather than one Spring Security saved after a real Cognito login; the JSON was produced by the same Jackson modules SessionConfiguration registers, but authorizedClientRegistrationId 'cognito' was never used by the app in this run.
  - The disable action was a direct `update users set enabled=false`; the app exposes no admin endpoint for it, so whatever tooling admins use in production was not part of the exercise.
  - DisabledUserStompInterceptor (STOMP frames on an already-open socket) was not exercised; only the /websocket HTTP filter chain was. Covered by DisabledUserStompInterceptorTest and WebSocketConfigurationInboundChannelTest.
  - The MGHEpicAuthController refusal of a disabled EHR-launch user was not exercised; covered by MGHEpicAuthControllerTest.
